text: Is Alicia's Law based on The Good Wife? Yes, it's the Mexican remake. Yes. "Alicia's Law" ("La Ley de Alicia") is a Mexican Netflix adaptation of the American legal drama "The Good Wife," which aired on CBS from 2009 to 2016. Fernanda Castillo stars as Alicia. Part 1 premieres on Netflix on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, and Part 2 arrives Dec. 9, 2026.. Part 1 of "Alicia's Law" premieres on Netflix on Nov. 11, 2026.. In the Netflix version, Alicia's life falls apart when her husband, Aurelio (Juan Manuel Bernal), a Supreme Court justice, is brought down by a public scandal. She returns to practicing law to support her two children and reconnects with David (Michel Brown), her college sweetheart, who now owns the firm where she works. The series is produced by CBS Studios with TIS Estudios and is set against Mexico's political landscape. The original "The Good Wife" ran seven seasons on CBS with Julianna Margulies in the lead role and won five Primetime Emmys from 43 nominations. Neither the original nor the Mexican remake is presented as a true story; both are fictional legal dramas.

What is the Edgar Martinez Award? MLB's best DH; 2026 winner Nov. 11. The Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter Award goes to MLB's best designated hitter each season. It has been given since the DH was introduced in 1973 and was renamed in 2004 for Hall of Famer Edgar Martinez, a five-time winner. The 2026 award will be presented on Wednesday, Nov. 11, at the MLB Awards on MLB Network.. The 2026 Edgar Martinez Award will be announced on Nov. 11, 2026, at the MLB Awards in Las Vegas.. Orlando Cepeda of the Boston Red Sox won the first award in 1973, and none was given in 1994. David Ortiz has the most wins with eight. Shohei Ohtani won it five straight times from 2021 to 2025, matching Ortiz's five-year streak from 2003 to 2007 and Martinez's career total of five. The 2026 winner will be revealed during the MLB Awards show in Las Vegas, which starts at 9 p.m. ET on MLB Network. The same show presents the All-MLB Teams, the Hank Aaron Awards, Comeback Player of the Year, the Rivera and Hoffman Reliever of the Year Awards and MLB Executive of the Year.

How is the speaker of the House elected? A roll-call vote of all members. The speaker of the House is elected by a roll-call vote of the full House on the first day of a new Congress. To win, a candidate needs an absolute majority of all votes cast for a person by name, which is usually 218 if every member votes. If no one gets a majority, the House votes again until someone does.. Democrats won control of the House in the Nov. 3, 2026, midterms, so the next speaker will be chosen when the new Congress convenes in January 2027.. According to the Congressional Research Service, "each new House elects a Speaker by roll call vote when it first convenes," and the vote is repeated until a candidate wins a majority. Because absences, vacancies and members voting "present" reduce the number of votes cast for named candidates, a speaker can win with fewer than 218 votes. Multiple ballots are rare: nine were needed in 1923, and 15 were needed in January 2023, when Kevin McCarthy was elected. The Constitution does not require the speaker to be a member of the House, but every speaker so far has been one. Before the floor vote, each party picks its nominee in a closed-door caucus or conference meeting. The floor vote for the 120th Congress is expected when it convenes, set by the 20th Amendment for Jan. 3, 2027. After Democrats won the House in the 2026 midterms, WSOC-TV reported that Rep. Hakeem Jeffries is the front-runner for speaker and that House Democrats are expected to hold their leadership elections in November.

What is a lame duck session? Congress returns Nov. 9 after the midterms. A lame duck session is any meeting of Congress held after the November election but before the new Congress takes office on Jan. 3. The outgoing members, not the newly elected ones, still cast the votes. The 2026 lame duck session begins Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, when both the House and Senate return.. Congress returns on Nov. 9, 2026, for its first session since the midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both the House and Senate.. The Congressional Research Service defines it simply: a lame duck session "occurs whenever one Congress meets after its successor is elected." The phrase "lame duck" was first used in 18th-century Britain for bankrupt businessmen and by the 1830s was applied to officeholders whose time in office had a known end date. The 20th Amendment, ratified in 1933, moved the start of each new Congress to Jan. 3, so since 1935 any meeting between the November election and Jan. 3 counts as a lame duck session. According to CRS, there were 25 such sessions from 1935 through 2024, and one has been held in every Congress since 1999-2000. Their main purpose is to finish legislation, most often government funding bills and program authorizations. For 2026, the House is scheduled to sit for two weeks starting Nov. 9, break for Thanksgiving week and then return until Dec. 17. The Senate sits Nov. 9 and 10, returns Nov. 16 for a week, breaks for Thanksgiving and comes back Nov. 30 for the first three weeks of December. The 120th Congress, elected on Nov. 3, 2026, begins at noon on Jan. 3, 2027.

What is the posting system in MLB? 2026 window closes Dec. 16. The posting system is how a player under contract with a Japanese (NPB) or Korean (KBO) team can sign with an MLB club. His team "posts" him, all 30 MLB teams can negotiate, and the signing club pays his old team a release fee. Japanese players get a 45-day window; Korean players get 30 days.. Japan's Teruaki Sato, Kaima Taira and Hiromi Itoh entered the MLB posting system on Nov. 2, 2026, with a signing deadline of Dec. 16.. Under MLB's agreements with NPB and the KBO, the release fee is 20% of the first $25 million of a major league contract, 17.5% of the next $25 million and 15% of anything above $50 million, plus a 15% supplemental fee on earned bonuses, escalators and exercised options. A deal must be signed by 5 p.m. ET on the final day of the window. If a player does not sign, he returns to his team for the next season and cannot be posted again until the following offseason. In November 2026, Hanshin Tigers infielder Teruaki Sato, Seibu Lions pitcher Kaima Taira and Nippon-Ham Fighters pitcher Hiromi Itoh were posted; their window runs until Dec. 16, 2026. Korean infielder Si-Hwan Roh of the Hanwha Eagles has a 30-day window that ends Dec. 1. MLB's labor contract with the players' union also expires Dec. 1, 2026; during the 2021-22 lockout, posted players were frozen and their windows resumed after the deal was reached on March 10, 2022.

What is the difference between Record of the Year and Song of the Year?. Record of the Year honors a specific recording, so it goes to the artist, producers, engineers, mixers and mastering engineers. Song of the Year honors the composition itself, so it goes to the songwriters. The same track can be nominated in both. The 2027 Grammy nominations will be announced on Monday, Nov. 16, 2026.. The Recording Academy will announce the 2027 Grammy nominations, including Record and Song of the Year, on Nov. 16, 2026.. According to the Recording Academy, Record of the Year recognizes "the best overall achievement" in a recording, including performance, production and engineering. Song of the Year recognizes "the best achievement in songwriting" and is open only to the songwriters of new material. A singer who did not write the song can win Record of the Year but not Song of the Year. The 2027 Grammys cover music released from Aug. 31, 2025, to Aug. 28, 2026. First-round voting ran from Oct. 12 to Oct. 22, 2026, and final-round voting runs from Dec. 10, 2026, to Jan. 7, 2027. The ceremony will be held on Sunday, Feb. 7, 2027, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and aired on ABC, Disney+ and Hulu.

Who was Richard Avedon? The photographer in Ron Howard's Netflix film. Richard Avedon (1923-2004) was an American fashion and portrait photographer who shot for Harper's Bazaar and Vogue and became The New Yorker's first staff photographer in 1992. He is the subject of "Avedon," a documentary directed by Ron Howard that arrives on Netflix on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026.. Ron Howard's documentary "Avedon" premieres on Netflix on Nov. 11, 2026.. Avedon was born in New York City on May 15, 1923, and died on Oct. 1, 2004, in San Antonio, Texas, while on assignment for The New Yorker. He joined Harper's Bazaar in 1944, moved to Vogue in 1965 and shot most of its covers from 1973 until 1988. His best-known images include "Dovima with Elephants" (1955), a print of which sold for a record £719,000 at Christie's in 2010, and "In the American West" (1985), a book of large-format portraits of working-class Americans. The photographer played by Fred Astaire in the 1957 film "Funny Face" was a fictionalized version of him. The Netflix documentary, which premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, runs 1 hour 44 minutes and draws on Avedon's personal archives, including unseen stills and behind-the-scenes footage. It was made by Imagine Documentaries and Fifth Season in association with the Richard Avedon Foundation, with Brian Grazer and Ron Howard among the producers.

What is the Silver Slugger Award? 2026 winners announced Nov. 17. The Silver Slugger Award goes to the best offensive player at each position in the American and National leagues. It has been presented since 1980 by Louisville Slugger maker Hillerich & Bradsby, and MLB managers and coaches vote. The 2026 winners will be announced on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026.. Louisville Slugger will announce the 2026 Silver Slugger winners on Nov. 17, 2026, after the finalists were revealed on Nov. 2.. Each team gets four votes, cast by its manager and three coaches, and voters cannot pick players from their own team. They weigh statistics such as OPS, OPS+, home runs, RBIs and batting average, along with "general impressions of a player's overall offensive value." Each league names 10 winners: catcher, first base, second base, third base, shortstop, three outfielders, designated hitter and a utility player, which was added in 2022. A team award for the best offensive club in each league began in 2023. The trophy is a three-foot bat plated with sterling silver. Barry Bonds holds the record with 12 Silver Sluggers; Mike Piazza and Alex Rodriguez have 10 each. The Silver Slugger is the hitting counterpart of the Gold Glove, which honors defense and was announced on Nov. 1, 2026. The 2026 Silver Slugger finalists were announced on Nov. 2.

Who is Teruaki Sato? Japan's Triple Crown slugger posted for MLB. Teruaki Sato is a 27-year-old left-handed-hitting third baseman for Japan's Hanshin Tigers who won the 2026 Central League Triple Crown. He was posted for MLB teams on Nov. 2, 2026, and all 30 clubs can negotiate with him until 5 p.m. ET on Dec. 16, 2026.. Sato entered the MLB posting system on Nov. 2, 2026, together with pitchers Kaima Taira and Hiromi Itoh.. Sato batted .306 with 39 home runs and 106 RBIs in 2026 to win the Triple Crown. In 2025 he was the Central League MVP with 40 homers, 102 RBIs and a .924 OPS, and he won the NPB Golden Glove for defense. Over a six-year NPB career he has an .851 OPS, has hit at least 20 homers in five seasons and has played at least 120 games every year. He also has 262 NPB games in the outfield. He helped Hanshin win the 2023 Japan Series and played for Japan at the 2026 World Baseball Classic. Because he is older than 25, Sato is not limited by international bonus-pool rules. The team that signs him pays Hanshin a release fee based on the size of his contract. Reporter Jon Heyman has linked the Mets, Yankees, Dodgers and Phillies to him. If he does not sign by Dec. 16, he returns to Hanshin for 2027.

When does the new Congress take office? Noon on Jan. 3, 2027. The new Congress takes office at noon on Sunday, Jan. 3, 2027. That is when the 120th Congress, elected in the Nov. 3, 2026, midterms, begins and the terms of the outgoing members end. The 20th Amendment sets Jan. 3 as the date, though Congress can choose a different day by law.. After the Nov. 3, 2026, midterms, in which the AP reported Democrats winning both the House and Senate, many are asking when the new majority actually takes over.. Section 1 of the 20th Amendment says the terms of senators and representatives end "at noon on the 3d day of January" and that "the terms of their successors shall then begin." Section 2 says Congress shall assemble at noon on Jan. 3 "unless they shall by law appoint a different day." Because Jan. 3, 2027, falls on a Sunday, the swearing-in could be moved by law; WSOC-TV noted that since 1995 the latest a Congress has been seated is Jan. 7 (in 1997 and 2003). Democrats won control of both chambers in the 2026 midterms. Until Jan. 3, the outgoing 119th Congress keeps working in a lame duck session that begins Nov. 9, 2026. On its first day, the new House elects a speaker; Rep. Hakeem Jeffries is the front-runner.
